PullRequest.Title: agentHost: Reconcile retained-child status after stale reads
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- Capture task-status freshness when `tasks.list` actually starts, rather than when the throttler queues it.
- Drain invalidated reads through the existing single-flight scheduler so a stable final revision reconciles without a rescue notification.
- Recheck freshness while applying completions and stop pending work on cancellation or disposal.
- Add six deterministic delayed-query/lifecycle regressions and include child turn IDs, states, responses, and active-turn state in retained-child E2E failures.

## Why

A retained-child resume advances the existing status revision. Previously, it could invalidate the last in-flight read without scheduling another one. A read queued before resume could also return current state and then discard it using its obsolete enqueue-time revision. The new gated-query tests reproduce both lost-completion paths on unchanged main.

The CI audit found five retained-child state assertion failures; a representative failure is [this Linux execution](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/34438163030/job/102747545318), followed by a [successful same-source rerun](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/34438163030/job/102765196641).

Related to #335458. That issue tracks duplicate child turns and is **not closed by this standalone PR**. Child execution identity and late-event start/resume classification remain separate work; the existing active-child set and resume revision integration are unchanged.

## Validation

- Before the production change: 4 passing / 3 failing in the initial targeted regression run.
- After the change: 9 focused reconciliation tests passing; 42 related tests passing (overlapping sets).
  ```powershell
  .\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\copilotAgentSession.test.ts --grep "subagent task status|stale idle status|resumed subagent when"
  .\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\copilotAgentSession.test.ts --grep "subagent|child|detached shell"
  ```
- Two strict, tokenless Windows source-Electron runs of the exact retained-child E2E: 1 passing each. Recording and snapshot-update flags were disabled and token environment variables cleared.
  ```powershell
  .\scripts\test-integration.bat --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\e2e\providers\copilotAgentHostE2E.integrationTest.ts --grep "retained background subagent completes repeated follow-up turns"
  ```
- Both runs preserve exactly one/two/three completed child turns containing `CHILD_INITIAL_DONE`, `CHILD_FOLLOWUP_ONE_DONE`, and `CHILD_FOLLOWUP_TWO_DONE`, with no active turn and the existing AHP snapshot unchanged.
- Targeted TypeScript dependency-closure check: 1,131 files, zero diagnostics. Targeted transpilation, ESLint, four-path hygiene, and `git diff --check` passed.

Scenarios.Scenario: Background task status notification reconciles retained subagent completion
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The SDK `session.background_tasks_changed` event queues reconciliation; the serialized `rpc.tasks.list` result must complete before terminal child states emit `subagent_completed` progress. This is on the child-status update path, not editor startup/render/input.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Lists authoritative SDK background tasks through `session.rpc.tasks.list()`.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One active call at a time. Notification bursts during an active call coalesce; at most one stable trailing list is needed after one or more invalidations, with further calls only if each read is invalidated again before completion.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same RPC ran for each active/coalesced reconciliation. The prior throttler already produced an active call plus one coalesced queued call for notification bursts, but a resume-only revision change could invalidate the active result without guaranteeing the trailing authoritative call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A stable list response is required before terminal subagent completion can be reconciled and published.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Frequency of background-task notifications and resumes while an RPC is in flight; task processing scales with the task list returned by the SDK. Effective RPC concurrency is one.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: `Throttler` enforces one active RPC. The new loop absorbs stale revisions serially, while any already queued throttler factory becomes a no-op once the reconciled revision catches up.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No result cache is used because status must be authoritative. Warm/cold behavior is the same; revisions coalesce invalidations, and only a stable final read is applied.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed loop, revision checks, throttler implementation, and deterministic call-count tests directly establish the call path and concurrency.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: SDK RPC duration and real notification burst frequency are not measured, but tests establish single-flight behavior and coalesced call counts.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The additional serialized read occurs only when an otherwise-lost resume invalidates a read, and preserves the prior active-plus-trailing cardinality for notification bursts.

Scenarios.Scenario: A status completion synchronously resumes another retained child while applying a task list
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Applying terminal tasks emits progress synchronously; a listener may resume another child and advance the revision. The current collection scan stops and a fresh authoritative task-list RPC must complete before applying the new stable state.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Repeats `rpc.tasks.list()` after the current result is invalidated during completion application.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One serialized retry for the resulting revision, coalescing multiple synchronous or queued invalidations; never concurrent.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The prior implementation continued applying the fetched collection without an intra-loop freshness check; if only the resume advanced freshness, it did not perform a required follow-up authoritative read.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The retry delays final completion reconciliation but prevents applying the remainder of a stale collection.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of distinct resume/status revisions that occur before each list response stabilizes, not raw task count or duplicate notifications after coalescing.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Strictly serialized by the existing `Throttler`; the test asserts maximum active calls of one.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is appropriate for this authoritative state transition. Duplicate invalidations share the newest revision and do not each force a call.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: production revision checks and the new two-child deterministic test prove the mechanism.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The prevalence of synchronous cross-child resumes is uncertain, but the extra boundary operation is limited to actual invalidation races.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The bounded extra RPC is necessary to replace stale data, and duplicates are coalesced rather than fanned out.

Scenarios.Scenario: Session abort or disposal while a task-status list call is pending
Scenarios.CriticalPath: An already-started SDK list call may finish, but cancellation/disposal checks prevent applying it or starting retry work. Session teardown does not wait for a new reconciliation loop iteration.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most the single already-active call; no trailing call after cancellation or disposal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: An in-flight list could also remain until its promise settled; the old post-await disposal check prevented application but had no abort-token check.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The existing in-flight operation is not newly cancellable, but the diff prevents additional list calls and completion processing after teardown.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One active reconciliation per session because of throttling; teardown does not scale retries with queued notifications.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One active RPC; cancellation/disposal terminates the loop and queued factories cannot issue another call for the captured canceled token.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache. Reconciled state is abandoned on teardown.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: token capture, loop guards, post-await checks, throttler disposal, and lifecycle tests establish the behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Underlying RPC cancellation support is not visible, but no changed line increases retained work after teardown.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression; cleanup behavior is improved by suppressing trailing work.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing test polls `subscribe` and, only while assertions fail, builds an expanded error message containing active-turn state and up to the expected one-to-three child turns. This affects test failure diagnostics, not product runtime.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Calls the existing test client's `subscribe` method once per polling attempt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Unchanged: one subscribe call per existing polling attempt, at 50 ms intervals for up to 100 attempts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same subscribe polling occurred and failures constructed a constant error string.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The boundary call already governed each E2E polling attempt; the diff only enriches a locally constructed failure message after the response.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: At most the test's expected one, two, or three turns per failure message and up to the existing bounded 100 polling attempts.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Sequential polling through the existing assertion helper; no new concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache; each poll intentionally requests current test state. The diff does not alter polling or subscription behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed hunk only maps turns and JSON-stringifies diagnostics after the existing subscribe result.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Markdown response size can vary, but this is bounded test-only failure work over at most three turns.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable product performance regression; added serialization is bounded and test-only.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance review of all four changed files and every diff page. The production change preserves single-flight/coalesced RPC behavior while adding only the authoritative trailing read required after a stale revision, and it stops retries on abort/disposal. Added trace and test diagnostic work does not establish a realistic user-facing performance regression. No findings submitted.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
